subject: SIG network follow-up: static egress IPs & private connectivity options
messages:

Cc: Jake Turner <itops@greenfield.health>

Subject: SIG: follow-up on network connectivity (private endpoints & static egress IPs)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for sending the initial SIG answers last week. We completed our internal review and have a couple of follow-ups specifically around network topology and egress controls before we can move to our security committee:

- Can Redwood support AWS PrivateLink or GCP Private Service Connect for private control-plane / API connectivity (no public internet exposure)?
- For hosted/Dedicated deployments, can you provide a published list of static egress IP addresses (per region) that we can allowlist?
- If static egress is not available, what are the recommended mitigations (e.g., NAT with Elastic IPs, proxy, TLS inspection notes)?
- Do you have an architecture diagram showing where PrivateLink/PSC and NAT egress sit relative to customer VPCs?

We attached our SIG worksheet with the specific question IDs marked. Ideally we’d get an answer and any evidence or diagrams by next week so we can close this out. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our platform security team.

Thanks,
Nina Morales
Head of Information Security
Greenfield Health

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on network connectivity (private endpoints & static egress IPs)

Hi Nina — great questions, thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary; I’ve attached a short tech note and a consolidated ZIP with the diagrams and CSV of egress ranges. We can hop on a call next week if you’d like to walk through.

Summary of options (high level):
- Private connectivity: Redwood supports private connectivity options in major clouds. On AWS we support AWS PrivateLink for control-plane and API endpoints; on GCP we support Private Service Connect. These provide an endpoint in your VPC so traffic never traverses the public internet.
- Static egress IPs (hosted + dedicated): For hosted customers we publish a set of regional egress IP ranges that are used by our outbound traffic; for Dedicated customers we can provision a dedicated egress pool backed by Elastic IPs (AWS) or static NAT gateways in the customer's region. See attached CSV for current published ranges.
- If static egress is not acceptable: recommended mitigations include using PrivateLink/PSC for all inbound/control-plane traffic, and using a customer-side NAT/proxy for outbound integrations. We also support setting up an outbound proxy within your VPC to terminate egress to third parties.

Evidence and attachments included:
- redwood_private_connectivity_options_v1.pdf — short architecture note (PrivateLink/PSC diagrams)
- egress_ip_ranges_20261020.csv — current published egress ranges by region (format: region, CIDR, notes)
- sig-network-answers-attachments.zip — diagrams and SOC/SIG references

Next steps: if you want, pick a 30-min slot and we’ll include our infra engineer (Sergio) to go deeper on NAT/eIP provisioning.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_private_connectivity_options_v1.pdf (PDF)]

Rishi / Kim — short answers: provisioning and IP details below. I’ve attached the CSV we plan to send to customers.

- Dedicated egress provisioning: typical lead time is 5–10 business days once legal/ops signs the SOW to cover the dedicated IPs and allocation. We allocate a pool of Elastic IPs and configure the NAT gateway in the requested region(s). We will document the configuration steps in the SOW and include change-control for future IP changes.
- Published CSV: current published outbound CIDRs (examples):
  - us-east-1: 34.198.0.0/16
  - us-west-2: 54.204.0.0/15
  - eu-west-1: 52.57.0.0/16
  - ap-southeast-1: 13.124.0.0/16

Note: some hosted ranges are shared across customers; for Dedicated we provide isolated Elastic IPs. The CSV attached has a per-region, per-network mapping and a notes column for rotation policy.

Attachment: egress_ip_ranges_20261020.csv

Sergio
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Private connectivity: We support AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect for control-plane/API endpoints. This ensures management and API calls do not traverse the public internet. See page 2 of the attached PDF for the diagram.
- Static egress IPs: attached CSV contains our published egress CIDRs by region. For Dedicated customers we can allocate a dedicated egress pool (Elastic IPs) — typical provisioning 5–10 business days after SOW.
